story-context.acceptanceCriteria: 1. Create `/src/bet_bot/data/fetchers/api_football.py` module 2. Initialize API client with `API_FOOTBALL_KEY` from config and proper headers 3. Implement `fetch_fixtures(date: str) -> list[Fixture]` function for fetching today's fixtures 4. Implement `fetch_team_form(team_id: str, league_id: str) -> TeamForm` function for team statistics 5. Implement `fetch_injuries(team_id: str) -> Injury` function for player availability data 6. Implement `fetch_odds(fixture_id: str) -> Odds` function for current betting odds 7. Add retry logic using tenacity (max 5 attempts, exponential backoff 2-60s) 8. Handle rate limiting: respect Retry-After headers, implement client-side rate limiter (100 req/min) 9. Map API-Football nested responses to Pydantic models using Field aliases 10. Log all API calls (URL, status, timestamp) and errors with context 11. All functions return data validated against Pydantic models or raise custom exceptions 12. Handle 4xx errors gracefully (404 → return None, 401/403 → raise APIAuthenticationError) 13. Handle 5xx errors with retry logic (up to 5 attempts) 14. Handle network/timeout errors gracefully (return None with logging)

doc.title: bet-bot Technical Specification
doc.snippet: Primary data source for fixtures, form, injuries, odds. Endpoints: /fixtures, /teams/statistics, /injuries, /odds. Rate limit: 300 requests/minute. Pricing: ~$15/month (paid tier). Must handle nested response structures.

doc.title: bet-bot Technical Specification
doc.snippet: Parallel async fetching from multiple APIs/scrapers. Key Pattern: async def fetch_all_data() using asyncio.gather(*tasks, return_exceptions=True). Error Handling: If API-Football fails → use scrape backup. If scrape fails → continue with missing data (graceful degradation).

doc.title: bet-bot Development Stories
doc.snippet: Set up API-Football client with proper authentication. Implement fetch_fixtures, fetch_team_form, fetch_injuries, fetch_odds functions. Add retry logic (3 attempts, exponential backoff). Handle rate limiting gracefully. Log all API calls (URL, response status, timestamp). Responses must map to Pydantic models.

doc.title: Project-Specific Claude Code Rules
doc.section: PYTHON API CLIENT IMPLEMENTATION - HTTP Client Architecture
doc.snippet: ALWAYS use httpx for sync/async compatibility. ALWAYS use a single global client instance with connection pooling. NEVER instantiate multiple client instances in hot loops. Standard Pattern: Global _http_client singleton with httpx.AsyncClient configuration (timeout=30s, connection pooling, HTTP/2 enabled).

doc.title: Project-Specific Claude Code Rules
doc.section: PYTHON API CLIENT IMPLEMENTATION - Retry Logic
doc.snippet: ALWAYS use tenacity library for retry logic. ALWAYS use exponential backoff with jitter. ALWAYS retry ONLY transient errors (5xx, timeouts, connection errors). NEVER retry 4xx errors (except 429 rate limit). Standard Retry Config: 5 attempts max, wait_exponential (2s, 4s, 8s, 16s, 32s max). Must respect Retry-After headers.

doc.title: Project-Specific Claude Code Rules
doc.section: PYTHON API CLIENT IMPLEMENTATION - Error Handling
doc.snippet: ALWAYS define custom exception hierarchy. Custom exceptions: BetBotError (base) → APIError → APIRateLimitError, APIAuthenticationError, APINotFoundError, APIServerError, DataValidationError, DataStaleError. ALWAYS include context in exceptions (url, status, response body). NEVER swallow exceptions silently.

doc.title: Project-Specific Claude Code Rules
doc.section: PYTHON API CLIENT IMPLEMENTATION - Response Validation
doc.snippet: ALWAYS validate response structure before processing. ALWAYS use Pydantic models for response parsing. ALWAYS handle missing fields gracefully. Standard Pattern: Use Field aliases for nested API responses (e.g., fixture_id = Field(..., alias="fixture.id")). Validate JSON deserialization with safe_json_parse.

doc.title: Story 2.1: Create Pydantic Models for Data Structures
doc.snippet: All models use Pydantic v2 with BaseModel and ConfigDict. Field aliases enabled for API-Football response mapping. Models include: Fixture (fixture_id aliased as "fixture.id"), Team, League, TeamForm, Injury, InjuredPlayer, Odds, Market. Team and League objects must be manually constructed from nested API structures.

story-context.constraints: - MANDATORY: Use httpx.AsyncClient singleton pattern with global _http_client instance (NEVER create multiple clients) - MANDATORY: Use tenacity library for retry logic with exponential backoff (2s, 4s, 8s, 16s, 32s max, 5 attempts) - MANDATORY: Only retry transient errors (5xx, timeouts, connection errors). NEVER retry 4xx except 429 rate limit - MANDATORY: Respect Retry-After headers from 429 responses (both seconds and HTTP date format) - MANDATORY: Implement client-side rate limiter using token bucket algorithm (100 requests/60s for API-Football) - MANDATORY: Define custom exception hierarchy (must create exceptions.py if not exists): BetBotError → APIError → specific error types - MANDATORY: All API responses MUST be validated with Pydantic models before returning - MANDATORY: Use Field aliases for nested API-Football structures (e.g., fixture.id, teams.home.name) - MANDATORY: Team and League objects must be manually constructed from nested API response data (not auto-mapped) - MANDATORY: Log all API calls with URL, status code, timestamp, and errors with full context - MANDATORY: Never log API keys (use config.get_masked_key() for safe logging) - MANDATORY: Return None for graceful degradation on 404, timeouts, network errors (NOT raise exception) - MANDATORY: Raise APIAuthenticationError for 401/403, APIRateLimitError for 429, APIServerError for 5xx - MANDATORY: Connection pooling: 100 max connections, 20 keepalive connections - MANDATORY: Timeout configuration: 30s total timeout, 10s connect timeout - MANDATORY: Enable HTTP/2 for better multiplexing performance - MANDATORY: All async functions must use proper error handling with try/except/finally - CODE STYLE: Follow existing Pydantic v2 patterns (ConfigDict, not deprecated Config class) - CODE STYLE: Use type hints for all function parameters and return types - CODE STYLE: Max line length 100 characters (configured in ruff) - CODE STYLE: Include comprehensive docstrings for all public functions - TESTING: Minimum 90% code coverage for new api_football.py module - TESTING: Mock httpx responses, test all error scenarios, validate Field alias mapping

tests.standards: This project uses pytest with pytest-asyncio for async test support and pytest-cov for coverage reporting. All tests are located in /tests/ directory. Test structure follows pattern: /tests/unit/test_{module_name}.py for unit tests, /tests/integration/test_{feature}.py for integration tests. Minimum 80% code coverage target project-wide, 90%+ for critical modules like API clients. Tests must mock external API calls using httpx.MockTransport or similar. All Pydantic model validation must be tested with both valid and invalid inputs.
